sites.T1: Both channels show two diagonal band arrangements and a near-transverse family crossing several red/yellow bodies. Rank changes preserve the same trio. Reflections contribute; no bead-center correspondence established.
sites.T2: Both channels recover comparable alternating bands across mixed red/yellow/black rows. Sigma20 fails, so the stable classification is 3/4, not width-invariant. Reflections and material contrast remain confounds.
sites.T3: Y provides a more distinct three-direction arrangement; both channels retain competing trios. Y 1/2/3 is the common development-like branch, while 1/3/4 remains an alternative. V splits the near-tangent reciprocal feature into close competitors and fails both width checks.
sites.T4: Raw beads change projected orientation through a bend. V 1/3/4 includes an approximately longitudinal spatial-band family (reciprocal about90deg), unlike the common branch. Y retains a bright low-frequency clipped competitor. Inverses have plausible stripes but no stable common three-family account.
sites.T5: Two diagonal row-like contributions remain visible in Y, but the remaining bright pair differs from the common near-tangent reciprocal family. Strong color/outline modulation and a prominent black reflection coexist. No supported primary trio; do not substitute successful Y sigma20 diagnostic.
sites.T6: Y separates a row-like near-transverse family and two diagonal families; rank4 is close to a harmonic of rank1. V is dominated by a broad clipped low-frequency contribution. Y support is stable3/4, failing sigma40; inverses still strongly emphasize highlights.
